# Generated by Claude Fable 5 (Anthropic)
Design — abstraction axes over the FISH graph (the "triangle" note, formalised)
================================================================================
Written 2026-08-21, from a discussion with Fatih (his handwritten note
~/Downloads/abstraction.jpeg + this conversation). Status: DEFINITIONS FIXED
(see "Fixed decisions" at the end); implementation NOT started. Companion to
notes/design_task_model_from_ft.txt (the IR these abstractions are views of).

Motivation
----------
The namespace-grouped component graph (Layer B) was received as "the most
abstract representation possible" — but it is one of THREE maximally abstract
representations. Fatih's note draws a triangle: CPU (EX-N-E-F), GPU (streams),
ROS namespaces — with the concrete graph in the middle and an "abstraction
slider" selecting how far a view is pulled toward a corner.

Core definitions (fixed)
------------------------
1. FACTS, not attribute values, are what we partition.
   The population is the set of execution instances in the IR: CPU callback
   executions (F instances) and GPU operations (kernel/memcpy launches and the
   CUDA API calls that submit them). Attribution (correlation_id, callback
   windows) equips EVERY fact with EVERY attribute: a kernel knows which
   callback, entity, node, namespace, executor submitted it; a callback knows
   which streams it submitted to, which TID ran it.

2. ABSTRACTION = an ordered list of grouping keys over the fact population.
   Grouping by a key prefix (k1), then (k1,k2), then (k1,k2,k3) … is a strict
   refinement chain REGARDLESS of the relation between the key domains.
   (Lemma: cumulative grouping keys always refine — many-to-many between,
   e.g., streams and TIDs is harmless, because we never partition streams by
   TIDs; we partition facts by the (stream, TID) pair.)

3. AXIS = a canonical key order.  SLIDER = the prefix length along an axis.
   The three canonical orders (each the other's reversal at the ends):

     OS  axis:  EX  → N → E → F → CUDA-API → TID → Stream
     GPU axis:  Stream → TID → CUDA-API → F → E → N → EX
     ROS axis:  ns¹ → ns² → … → N → E → F → (open toward CUDA at the bottom,
                                             open toward wider grouping at top)

   "Roots and leaves swap between views" (Fatih's tri-partite intuition)
   = permuting the key order. The chains cross the CPU/GPU type boundary
   without breaking because facts carry all attributes (definition 1).

4. TRIANGLE INTERIOR = mixing prefixes from two (or three) axes = the union
   of their key lists (a meet in the partition lattice). Example:
   (EX) × (ns¹) = "which executor serves which subsystem" matrix. Comes for
   free from definition 2.

5. EDGES SURVIVE THE QUOTIENT. Facts are not independent rows (this is what
   separates us from plain OLAP): message / state / join edges with their
   per-instance measurements live between facts. A quotient maps edge
   endpoints to classes; edge KINDS are never merged (parallel edges per
   kind: trigger / sampled / join / infra), numeric aggregation must be
   computed from pooled instances (percentile of the pool, NOT median of
   medians) or be explicitly labelled approximate.
   Intra-class edges become the class's INTERNAL SUMMARY ("147 hops ·
   9 state reads"), not self-loop clutter.

6. SELECTION ≠ ABSTRACTION, and their order is fixed: filters (drop init /
   zero_exec / infra / ext) are a selection σ applied FIRST; the quotient π
   applies to the selected subgraph. (σ∘π ≠ π∘σ; we standardise on σ first —
   the current behaviour of every view.)

7. Two kinds of partitions, epistemically distinct:
   - label-driven (the three axes): the designer's / the machine's declared
     structure;
   - connectivity-driven (FTs = WCCs over data edges): structure DISCOVERED
     by measurement. FTs sit OUTSIDE the axis scheme (no refinement chain of
     FTs exists) and stay a separate view family.

Naming anchor (literature)
--------------------------
This is a dimensional model (OLAP star schema) built ON TOP of a graph:
fact table + dimension hierarchies, slider = roll-up/drill-down, re-rooting
= pivot. The novel part is (5): facts are graph vertices with measured
communication edges, and quotients transport the edges — "graph-valued
OLAP". Plus (7): emergent partitions no dimension supplies.

Display consequence (many-to-many is a finding, not a bug)
----------------------------------------------------------
Nested-box rendering is duplication-free only where consecutive keys are
many-to-one. Where they are not (a node whose callback groups sit in two
executors; a TID feeding two streams), the inner box is DUPLICATED under
both parents, visibly marked (⧉). The duplication is exactly the
design/deployment mismatch — the address of interference — and must be
shown, not hidden. Empirical pre-checks per session (verifiable from PG):
does any node span executors? does any stream receive from multiple TIDs?

Relating the existing views (σ, keys, measurement projection)
-------------------------------------------------------------
  FT view          σ=data-phase, π=WCC(data edges)         hop/age per edge
  Layer B          σ=data-phase, π=(ns¹)                   trigger/sampled, p50
  NS views (FT pg) σ=data-phase, π=(ns^k), k=1..3          same, per namespace
  gantt-tid        σ=all,        π=identity, keys=(pid,TID) time axis
  gantt-cb         σ=all,        π=identity, keys=(cb)      time axis
  cb-stats         σ=all,        π=(F)                      count statistics
  → the OS corner (EX-grouped component graph) and the GPU corner
    (stream-grouped) are EMPTY today; the slider exists only on the ROS axis
    (ns_depth 1–3). That is the gap this design fills.

Fixed decisions (2026-08-21, Fatih)
-----------------------------------
[F1] Definition adopted verbatim: "abstraction = ordered key list over the
     fact population; axis = canonical order; slider = prefix length".
     Triangle interior = key-list union (def. 4).
[F2] Chain ends: OS axis ends at Stream; GPU axis ends at EX (symmetric,
     each the other's reversal); ROS axis stays OPEN at both ends
     (up toward coarser naming, down toward CUDA).
[F3] Terminology stays axis / level / pivot FOR NOW; RTS-aligned names are
     to be chosen only after the problem is fully solved.

Open (not yet decided)
----------------------
- Pooled-percentile aggregation everywhere vs per-edge summaries labelled
  approximate (cost/precision trade-off) — must also AUDIT the current
  Layer B multi-topic link p50 under this rule before building on it.
- Which meets (axis mixtures) are first-class UI (EX × ns matrix?) vs
  constructible-on-demand.
- Where CUDA-API sits exactly: partition level of GPU facts vs expansion of
  F (both sound; pick per use).
